derived_checks.note: These ratios compare non-synchronized providers with different contract/exchange coverage. They are data-quality diagnostics, not estimates of one canonical OI value.

event_timeline.event: Binance XRP Ledger hot-wallet incident; approximately 233.46M XRP reported stolen from five Binance-attributed wallets.
Binance Recovery Update #4 lists XRP withdrawals on the XRP network in phase one; the announcement says assets are reopened progressively after security checks.
Reuters reports additional withdrawal services across BSC, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Sui networks effective 04:00 GMT, but does not specify which individual assets are available on each network.

corrections: Do not say native XRP withdrawals were first restored on November 3: Binance's official November 1 phase-one update already listed XRP on the XRP network.
The November 3 Reuters report may concern additional assets on the XRP network; asset-by-network mapping is not specified.
Do not infer stolen XRP sales from exchange withdrawals or from OI changes without transaction-level linkage.

hypotheses.statement: The 2.4x open-interest spread is mainly coverage/contract-definition and aggregation methodology, not a real economic discrepancy.
hypotheses.next_test: Reconcile raw contract IDs, contract multipliers, USD conversion timestamps, venue coverage and inclusion of USDT/USDC contracts at one pinned cutoff.

hypotheses.statement: Positive aggregate funding and 77.6% long-account share indicate crowded long positioning, but do not establish net notional leverage or direction.
hypotheses.next_test: Collect notional long/short exposure, top-trader positions, liquidation depth, spot/perp basis and order-book depth.

hypotheses.statement: Binance withdrawal restoration could redistribute venue activity, but there is no evidence in these snapshots that XRP volume or OI migrated to competitors.
hypotheses.next_test: Compare synchronized Binance, Bybit, OKX, Coinbase, Kraken and on-chain exchange-tagged flows before/after each withdrawal phase.

data_quality: Provider timestamps differ by up to 81 minutes; no synchronized snapshot exists.
TradRadar's OI coverage is seven exchanges; Kodexius covers seven contracts across five exchanges; JustScreener covers nine exchanges. These scopes are not equivalent.
Funding rates are exchange- and contract-specific; settlement intervals must be retained.
Long/short ratios count accounts, not notional exposure.
Liquidation data is partial: TradRadar says at least $2.68M across five exchanges.
Mark price is not spot price.
No canonical OI total is selected and no averaging is performed.
